name: IBPS RRB (Officer Scale I & Office Assistant)
tagline: Officer Scale I (PO) and Office Assistant (Multipurpose) jobs in Regional Rural Banks

overview.about: IBPS conducts the CRP-RRBs for Regional Rural Banks. Office Assistants are selected through Prelims and Mains (no interview); Officer Scale I candidates go through Prelims, Mains and an interview. Prelims has only Reasoning and Quant in 45 minutes, and Mains can be taken in English or Hindi.
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline (agriculture, horticulture, forestry, animal husbandry, veterinary, agri-engineering, pisciculture, agri-marketing, cooperation, IT, management, law, economics or accountancy are preferred for Officer Scale I)
Office Assistant: age 18–28 years; Officer Scale I: age 18–30 years; relaxation SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10 yrs
Proficiency in the local language of the participating RRB

pattern.note: No separate sectional timing; −0.25 per wrong answer

pattern.paper: Prelims (both posts) — Quantitative Aptitude / Numerical Ability

pattern.note: Same structure for Officer Scale I and Office Assistant
Final = Mains 80 : Interview 20; Office Assistant merit is Mains only

chapters.title: Officer Scale I vs Office Assistant: pattern & strategy

cards.title: Two posts, one syllabus
cards.body: Both posts share the same subject list. **Office Assistant** (clerk): Prelims → Mains → language test, no interview. **Officer Scale I** (PO): Prelims → Mains → interview (80 : 20). You may apply for both; exams are held on different days.

cards.title: 45-minute composite Prelims
cards.body: Prelims has **only Reasoning and Quant**, 80 questions in **45 minutes** with no sectional timer. That is about **34 seconds per question**. You choose how to split time, so a tested plan is essential.

cards.title: Prelims plan
cards.body: Typical split: Reasoning 22–24 min, Quant 20–22 min. Start with your stronger section. In Reasoning, do inequality, syllogism, coding and direction before the big puzzles; in Quant, do simplification/approximation and series first.

cards.title: Mains: 200 questions in 120 minutes
cards.body: Mains is a composite **2-hour** paper with 200 questions, about 36 seconds each. Computer (40 Q for 20 marks) and GA can be done fast; save the rest of the time for Reasoning and Quant (50 marks each).

cards.title: Hindi option
cards.body: In Mains you can take the language section in **English or Hindi**. Pick the one in which you read faster and make fewer grammar mistakes. The question paper itself is bilingual for other sections.

cards.q: IBPS RRB Prelims has 80 questions in 45 minutes. Average time per question is closest to:
Which RRB post has an interview?
cards.explain: Officer Scale I has an interview (weighted 20%); Office Assistant selection is on Mains marks.

cards.q: The Computer Knowledge section in RRB Mains carries:
cards.explain: Computer Knowledge has 40 questions worth 20 marks (0.5 each).

chapters.title: Rural banking awareness (RRBs, NABARD, KCC, PSL)

cards.title: RRB basics
cards.body: RRBs were set up from **2 October 1975** to serve small farmers, labourers and rural artisans; governed by the **RRB Act, 1976**. Ownership **Centre 50 : sponsor bank 35 : state 15**. **NABARD** supervises RRBs; RBI regulates them.

cards.title: Consolidation
cards.body: RRBs were merged in phases from 196 to 43, and under **'One State, One RRB'** (effective **1 May 2025**) to **28 RRBs**. The aim: stronger capital, technology and scale.

cards.title: NABARD
cards.body: Set up on **12 July 1982** on the recommendation of the **CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman) committee**. It refinances banks for agriculture and rural lending, manages the **RIDF**, and supervises RRBs and cooperative banks. HQ: Mumbai.

cards.title: Priority sector lending targets
points: RRBs and small finance banks: 75% of ANBC
Shortfall goes to RIDF and similar funds

cards.title: Kisan Credit Card
cards.body: Introduced in **1998** (R.V. Gupta committee) for timely short-term crop credit. Under the interest subvention scheme, eligible farmers get loans at **7%**, falling to an effective **4%** with prompt repayment. Budget 2025-26 raised the subvention limit from ₹3 lakh to **₹5 lakh**.

cards.q: Which body supervises Regional Rural Banks?
cards.explain: RBI regulates RRBs, but supervision is delegated to NABARD.

cards.q: The priority sector lending target for RRBs is:
cards.explain: RRBs (like small finance banks) must lend 75% of ANBC to priority sectors.
NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982.

chapters.title: Local language & Office Assistant provisional allotment

cards.title: Language proficiency
cards.body: Each RRB serves a specific state, so candidates must be proficient in that state's local language. For Office Assistants, a **language proficiency test** is held before final allotment; it is **qualifying**.

cards.title: Practise early
cards.body: Read local-language newspapers for 15 minutes daily and practise simple banking conversations. Many candidates lose their allotment here even after clearing Mains.

cards.title: Merit and allotment
cards.body: Office Assistant: **Mains marks only**, state-wise. Officer Scale I: Mains + interview at **80 : 20**. Allotment to an RRB depends on merit, vacancies and your preferences.

cards.title: Interview for Officer Scale I
cards.body: Expect rural-economy questions: KCC, crop seasons, PM-KISAN, self-help groups, priority sector lending and why you want to work in a rural branch. Know the RRB(s) of your state by name.

cards.q: For IBPS RRB Office Assistant, the local language test is:
cards.explain: It is a qualifying test held before final allotment.
